name: Svante August Arrhenius
summary: Swedish chemist and physicist, Nobel laureate in Chemistry (1903) for ionic theory of dissociation.

name: Vik
summary: Location near Uppsala, Sweden, birthplace of Svante Arrhenius.

name: Uppsala
summary: City in Sweden, location of the university where Arrhenius studied.

name: University of Uppsala
summary: Swedish university where Arrhenius completed undergraduate studies and doctoral dissertation.

name: Stockholm
summary: Capital city of Sweden, where Arrhenius worked and died.

name: Stockholm College
summary: Private institution for scientific studies in Stockholm, later renamed Stockholm University.

name: Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
summary: Swedish academy that awarded Arrhenius a travel grant and oversaw the Nobel Institute.

name: Nobel Institute for Physical Chemistry
summary: Research institute in Stockholm directed by Arrhenius from 1905.

name: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1903
summary: Nobel Prize awarded to Arrhenius for his ionic theory of dissociation.

name: Lehrbuch der kosmischen Physik
summary: Textbook on cosmical physics published by Arrhenius in 1903.

name: Worlds in the Making
summary: Best-selling book by Arrhenius on cosmological speculations, published in 1908.

name: Nobel Committee for Physics
summary: Committee of which Arrhenius was a member from 1900.

name: Physics Society
summary: Society established by Arrhenius in 1891 to promote physics discussions.

aliases: 1904 Congress of Arts and Science in St. Louis
name: Congress of Arts and Science 1904
summary: Congress in St. Louis where Arrhenius gave a lecture on cosmical physics.
